zebralogic.title: PreserveExactCase
zebralogic.principle: Copy every attribute value exactly as it appears in the puzzle, preserving case, spacing, and punctuation.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever outputting attribute values in the final solution JSON.
zebralogic.example: Writing "Swedish" or "swedish" when the puzzle lists the value as "swede".

zebralogic.title: DirectAdjacency
zebralogic.principle: Interpret clues stating "X is directly left of Y" as X's house number = Y's house number − 1 (and similarly for right).
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions a direct left/right relationship.
zebralogic.example: Treating "directly left of" as any left adjacency instead of the immediate neighbor.

zebralogic.title: RelativeOrdering
zebralogic.principle: Treat clues that say "X is somewhere to the left of Y" as a strict ordering constraint X < Y (and similarly for right).
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue indicates a relative left/right position without specifying distance.
zebralogic.example: Allowing X to be to the right of Y when the clue says X is somewhere to the left of Y.

zebralogic.title: AdjacencyWithoutOrientation
zebralogic.principle: Interpret clues stating "X and Y are next to each other" as |X − Y| = 1, with no implied left/right orientation.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions adjacency but does not specify direction.
zebralogic.example: Assuming X must be left of Y when the clue only says they are next to each other.

zebralogic.title: EquivalenceLinking
zebralogic.principle: When a clue states that two attribute values refer to the same entity, link them as a combined attribute (e.g., "The Swedish person is Peter" links nationality Swedish with name Peter).
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue equates two attribute values across categories.
zebralogic.example: Failing to link "Swedish" and "Peter", treating them as unrelated.

zebralogic.title: FixedHouseAssignment
zebralogic.principle: If a clue fixes an attribute to a specific house number, assign that attribute to that house immediately.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions a concrete house index (e.g., "The Dane is in the second house").
zebralogic.example: Leaving the Dane unassigned despite the clue that places the Dane in house 2.

zebralogic.title: ValidateJSONStructureAndSyntax
zebralogic.principle: Ensure the final JSON output is syntactically valid: all arrays and objects are properly closed, keys quoted, and no stray commas.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Before returning the final answer to the verifier.
zebralogic.example: Missing a closing bracket in the JSON, causing a parse error.

zebralogic.title: ChildAttributeLinking
zebralogic.principle: When a clue mentions a child's name, bind that child to the correct parent attribute (e.g., nationality, name) before assigning other attributes.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever clues involve children and their parents.
zebralogic.example: Assigning the wrong nationality to the mother of Timothy.

zebralogic.title: CompactFinalAnswer
zebralogic.principle: Output the solution JSON as the very last part of the response and keep any preceding reasoning concise.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When constructing the final answer for the verifier.
zebralogic.example: Placing explanatory text after the JSON, causing the parser to miss the solution.

zebralogic.title: OverlappingCategoryDisambiguation
zebralogic.principle: When attribute values appear in multiple categories (e.g., "cat" in both Animal and Pet), determine which category a clue refers to based on contextual keywords (owner, pet, lover, keeper, enthusiast) and treat each category independently, preserving uniqueness within each.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue mentions a term that exists in more than one attribute set.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting "cat lover" as referring to the Pet category instead of the Animal category, leading to a violation of the adjacency constraint.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model copies values without preserving the exact case, spacing, or spelling used in the puzzle.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Copy every attribute value verbatim from the puzzle description, preserving case, spaces, and punctuation.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model focuses on a subset of clues and fails to enforce all given constraints during assignment.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Systematically enumerate every clue, and after each tentative assignment verify that all constraints remain satisfied.

zebralogic.description: Malformed JSON due to missing closing brackets
zebralogic.why_it_happens: During generation the model loses track of nesting or truncates output, producing syntactically invalid JSON.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Generate the JSON structure incrementally, double‑check that every opening bracket has a matching closing one before finalizing.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model confuses which parent attribute (name, nationality, etc.) a child belongs to, leading to mismatched pairings.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: When a clue mentions a child, first bind the child's name to the correct parent attribute, then propagate that information to other attributes.

zebralogic.description: Incorrect disambiguation of overlapping attribute categories
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model assumes identical strings belong to the same attribute category, ignoring contextual cues that indicate a different category.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Identify the relevant attribute set for each term based on clue wording (e.g., "owner" → Animal, "pet" → Pet) and keep the categories separate even if they share literal values.
